name: Def Leppard Hysteria
reference: Pour Some Sugar on Me (~85 BPM) / Armageddon It (~120 BPM): Def Leppard, Hysteria (1987, prod. Mutt Lange)
rig: Lange moved Collen and Clark from Marshalls to custom-modified Tom Scholz Rockman headphone amps (Scholz changed the distortion and turned the chorus and reverb off), because 15-16 guitar tracks of Marshalls wouldn't fit; Nigel Green also used a JHS Rock Box and sometimes a Roland studio flanger on power chords. Collen: 'Felix', a '78 Japanese Strat with a DiMarzio Super Distortion; Clark: a three-pickup Les Paul
notes: Amp = Slammin MXR/Rockman X100, Distortion mode at half. The Rockman's output is cab-simulated and it was a headphone amp, so the cab slot is empty (recording direct is an inference). Spread with only 0.15 wobble (the chorus was off; the only documented modulation is Green's occasional flanger) plus Align wobble 0.2 for the layering. SW8 BOOST = TS9 push (not on the record); SW9 DELAY = 529 ms solo echo (dotted eighth at Pour Some Sugar's 85 BPM; Armageddon It would be 375 ms), off by default: no echo is documented on the parts. Research: the 80s-tones.md shortlist (captures and model ids checked with `tone3000.py models`). On the board (bank 1): SW8 = BOOST (slot 1), SW9 = DELAY (slot 5 / R3). Levels are unmeasured.

left.label: Ibanez TS9 clean push, D0 T6 L10 (lead boost, not on the record)
Dotted-eighth delay 529 ms (Pour Some Sugar, 85 BPM)
